original_test_intent: Read the system's persistent BIOS boot order through Redfish and verify the ordered boot-device sequence matches the platform specification.
original_method: Discover the target ComputerSystem, validate its Boot object and BootOrder representation, resolve each ordered token to an approved device identity, and compare the normalized sequence with a versioned oracle without modifying boot state.
manual_activity: Provide the firmware-matched System/Boot schema, expected ordered boot sequence and stable mapping for Redfish BootOrder tokens to BIOS/device identities, including disabled, absent and firmware-generated entry policy.
required_inputs: Boot token to device identity mapping
safety_requirements: No hardcoded credentials or TLS bypass
Never PATCH BootOrder or BIOS attributes
Preserve raw token order before normalization
Fail closed on unresolved, duplicate or wrong-system entries
agent_execution_scope: Bind BMC, system, BIOS and firmware
Validate Boot schema and ordered representation
Load the approved order and identifier map
Use secret-backed read-only access over verified TLS
Capture status and complete Boot object
Report unresolved or duplicate entries explicitly
engineer_actions: Provide endpoint/schema, expected order and identity map
Confirm persistent order only and no override/reboot scope

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: BootOrder is relevant, but the command hardcodes SystemId, bypasses TLS, strips other Boot context and compares neither order nor resolved device identities with an oracle.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Follow the advertised ComputerSystem URI, securely retain the complete Boot object, resolve ordered tokens through the approved device map and compare the semantic sequence with the versioned BIOS boot-order oracle.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The BIOS Boot Order read-only scope and 15/10 timing remain; SystemId, expected sequence, token mapping and exceptional-entry policy are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use an order-preserving token resolver that reports both raw Redfish identifiers and mapped BIOS/device identities before a deterministic sequence comparison.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces a projected array and unconditional YES with resource discovery, an external ordered oracle, identifier resolution and explicit separation from one-time override and writes.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Validates configured order as reported by Redfish only; it does not prove actual boot selection, device bootability, BIOS UI rendering, override behavior or persistence across reboot.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Opaque or firmware-generated tokens can change between builds, and exposing device paths may reveal storage topology; unresolved tokens cannot be silently ignored.

project_override_considerations: If the platform uses alias strings, UEFI device paths or OEM mappings, preserve raw Redfish values and use only the approved firmware-specific identity map. Do not substitute BootSourceOverrideTarget for persistent BootOrder.
expected_evidence: Advertised ComputerSystem URI and Boot schema
HTTP status and complete redacted Boot response hash
Raw ordered tokens and resolved device identities
Semantic sequence comparison and exact mismatch position

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, generic read-only Procedure and specification-match Criteria consistently call for BIOS Boot Order inspection. The absent endpoint, order and mapping are incomplete rather than contradictory.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The Boot schema, ordered oracle and identifier map are definable package inputs, so the case is REQUIRES rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Makes order comparison semantic and auditable, preventing opaque token arrays or one-time override fields from being mistaken for the specified persistent BIOS order.
independent_technical_reasoning: Boot order is an ordered relation, so set equality is insufficient and duplicates or unresolved tokens matter. Redfish implementations may expose persistent BootOrder alongside one-time BootSourceOverride fields; those are not interchangeable. Device tokens can be opaque aliases or UEFI paths that require a firmware-specific identity map before comparison. Although the read is low impact, any attempted correction, override or reboot would materially affect availability and lies outside this testcase.
